einstellungen.text: An old man has been sitting alone in the dark for two days. And nobody has checked on him.
It's your grandpa. You walked all day to get to him.
Grandpa is sitting in the living room. One candle. One crossword puzzle. That's it.
Lina throws her arms around his neck. Grandpa laughs. And coughs. And laughs again.
“Oh, kids. Radio silence is nothing new for me.”
“Nobody rings for me anyway. Not the phone. Not the doorbell either.”
That hits you right in the chest. Because he's right.
You see him on birthdays. At Christmas. Maybe at Easter.
If things stay like this, you might see him forty more times. Forty afternoons. That's it.
And every week that goes by never comes back. Not for Grandpa either.
Outside, it's getting dark. The second storm isn't far off.
Lina asks about the heart pills. Grandpa waves it off. “I've got two left. That's enough.”
Two pills. Today and tomorrow. And without computers, the pharmacies are closed.
Ben doesn't say anything. But he's thinking the same thing you are.
You sit down with him. Grandpa tells stories from the old days.
In the middle of a sentence, he stops talking.
His face turns gray. He grabs his chest. And slowly sinks into the armchair.
